newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Demand seen draining gasoline in API data.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Demand seen draining gasoline in API data.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
UTILIZATION..... DN 0.75 PCT PT 96.1 DN 0.60 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
Gasoline inventories are expected to show a decline for the sixth consecutive week in American Petroleum Institute's (API) oil stock data as gasoline demand continues at a feverish pitch.
Gasoline stocks are seen dropping between one and two million barrels, bringing total gasoline supply near an historically low level of 190 million barrels.
Crude stocks are expected to rise about two to three million barrels. Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, are seen growing by one to two million barrels.
Although there have been refinery snags in the past week, curtailed refinery output is not entirely blamed for the dwindling gasoline supply.
"We will have good (gasoline) demand. The cat cracker problems may not necessarily show up in this report yet," Ed Kevelson, director of refined products for Paribas Futures in New York.
The data, to be released Tuesday evening, will reflect the week ended August 1. Over the past month, the data's implied gasoline demand has averaged a torrid 8.7 million barrels per day (bpd).
